tenant.identity_basis: The appellant is the subtenant who became the direct tenant and filed the Section 8 petition.

landlord.identity_basis: The original landlord who accepted the appellant as a direct tenant.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi
property.identity_basis: The demised premises let to the appellant.

commencement_date.identity_basis: The date the agreement was reached and tenancy commenced as direct tenant.

evidence.proposition: The premises were let directly by the landlord to the particular applicant tenant with the relevant tenancy commencing after the commencement of the Act.
evidence.application: The court recounts that the appellant and landlord reached an agreement on June 20/22, 1955 to become direct tenants effective May 1, 1955.

R01.P1.basis: Supreme Court's factual reconstruction of the direct tenancy commencement.

petition.identity_basis: The petition filed for determination of standard rent.

commencement_date.identity_basis: The tenancy commencement date used for limitation calculation.

filing_date.identity_basis: The date the petition was filed.

evidence.proposition: The applicant filed the Section 8 petition within six months from commencement of that applicant's relevant tenancy.
evidence.application: The court notes the petition was filed on October 10, 1955, which is within six months of May 1, 1955.

R01.P2.basis: Supreme Court's acceptance of the trial court's timeline based on the direct tenancy date.

head_tenant.identity_basis: The head tenant who inducted the appellant as subtenant.

subtenant.identity_basis: The appellant was inducted as subtenant.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi
property.identity_basis: The premises involved in the subtenancy.

induction_date.identity_basis: The date of induction as subtenant.

evidence.proposition: The head tenant inducted the appellant as subtenant after the Act commenced.
evidence.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
evidence.application: The court states the appellant was inducted as a subtenant on September 1, 1954, after the Act's commencement.

R02.P1.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
R02.P1.basis: Supreme Court's factual finding regarding the subtenancy induction.

subtenant.identity_basis: The appellant was inducted without written consent.

landlord.identity_basis: The landlord whose consent was required.

written_consent_document.identity_basis: No evidence of written consent exists.

evidence.proposition: The record contains no evidence showing that the landlord gave written consent to the appellant's induction as subtenant.
evidence.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
evidence.application: The court explicitly states there is no evidence to show the appellant was inducted with the written consent of the landlord.

R02.P2.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
R02.P2.basis: Supreme Court's evidentiary assessment that no written consent was proven.

tenant.identity_basis: The appellant became the direct tenant.

landlord.identity_basis: The landlord who accepted the appellant.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi

effective_date.identity_basis: The date the direct tenancy became effective.

evidence.proposition: After Brook surrendered the head tenancy, the landlord expressly accepted the appellant as direct tenant from May 1, 1955.
evidence.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
evidence.application: The court confirms the appellant and landlord reached an agreement to become direct tenants effective May 1, 1955, after Brook's surrender.

R02.P3.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
R02.P3.basis: Supreme Court's recognition of the direct tenancy commencement date.

tenant.identity_basis: The appellant was the subject of the lower court's reasoning.

earlier_letting_date.identity_basis: The date used by lower courts as the start of limitation.

interpreting_courts.identity_basis: The courts that adopted the rejected construction.

evidence.proposition: The District Judge adopted the earlier subtenancy or first letting as the starting point for calculating the appellant's limitation period, and the High Court substantially endorsed that reasoning.
evidence.application: The District Judge held the petition barred because the tenancy commenced on Sept 1, 1954, and the High Court agreed with this view.

R03.P1.basis: Reported reasoning of the District Judge and High Court which was later rejected.

applicant.identity_basis: The appellant was the applicant in the limitation dispute.

earlier_event.identity_basis: The event proposed as the controlling letting.

later_event.value: Recognition as direct tenant on May 1, 1955
later_event.identity_basis: The later event of direct tenancy recognition.

governing_limitation_date.identity_basis: The date proposed by lower courts as the governing date.

evidence.proposition: The September 1, 1954 induction as Brook's subtenant is legally the controlling letting for the appellant's Section 11(b) application after direct tenancy was recognized from May 1, 1955.
evidence.application: The lower courts held that the subtenancy date controlled the limitation period, a view the Supreme Court rejected.

R03.P2.basis: Reported reasoning of the lower courts which was expressly rejected by the Supreme Court.

tenant.identity_basis: The appellant is the tenant paying rent.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi

contractual_monthly_rent.identity_basis: The agreed monthly rent stated in the plaint and agreement.

evidence.proposition: The evidence establishes an exact, consistent contractual monthly rent for the demised cottage under the direct tenancy.
evidence.application: The court notes the agreement was for a monthly rent of Rs. 277.50 (or Rs. 269.50 in one citation, but consistently cited as the agreed rate).

R04.P1.basis: Supreme Court's acknowledgment of the contractual rent amount.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi
property.identity_basis: The property for which standard rent was determined.

operative_standard_rent.identity_basis: The standard rent fixed by the trial court.

contractual_rent.identity_basis: The contractual rent to be compared.

evidence.proposition: The legally operative standard rent for the demised cottage has been established through the required adjudication, allowing comparison with the contractual amount.
evidence.application: The trial court fixed the standard rent at Rs. 855/- p.a., which the Supreme Court noted was remanded for final determination.

R04.P2.basis: Trial court's finding on standard rent, acknowledged by the Supreme Court as the basis for remand.

landlord.identity_basis: The landlord who filed the eviction suit.

tenant.identity_basis: The tenant who was sued for eviction.

notice_date.identity_basis: The date of the demand notice served.

suit.identity_basis: The eviction suit filed by the landlord.

evidence.proposition: The landlord brought a possession suit asserting failure to pay rent after the statutory demand notice under Section 13(1)(a).
evidence.application: The landlord filed Civil Suit No. 231/56 on July 3, 1956, seeking eviction under Section 13(1)(a) for default in rent after a notice dated May 10, 1956.

R05.P1.basis: Reported facts of the landlord's suit and notice.

lawful_arrears.identity_basis: The arrears claimed by the landlord.

notice_date.identity_basis: The date of the notice triggering the one-month period.

payment_or_tender_date.value: 1st day of hearing in the trial court
payment_or_tender_date.identity_basis: The date the tenant deposited the arrears.

evidence.proposition: The underlying statutory default occurred: the tenant neither paid nor tendered all legally payable arrears within one month after service of the qualifying demand notice.
evidence.application: The court recounts that the tenant deposited the arrears on the first day of the hearing, which was after the one-month period from May 10, 1956.

R05.P2.basis: Supreme Court's factual reconstruction of the timeline of deposit vs. notice.

tenant.identity_basis: The tenant who made the deposit.

deposit.value: All arrears claimed by the landlord
deposit.identity_basis: The amount deposited by the tenant.

deposit_date.value: 1st day of hearing in the trial court

evidence.proposition: During the eviction proceedings, the tenant deposited the arrears claimed by the landlord.
evidence.application: The court states that along with filing the written statement, the appellant deposited all the arrears of rent as claimed by the plaintiff-landlord.

R05.P3.basis: Supreme Court's factual finding that the tenant did deposit the arrears, albeit late.

coverage_limits: The judgment does not definitively establish the exact amount of arrears deposited, only that 'all arrears claimed' were deposited.
The specific date of the hearing where the deposit was made is not explicitly given as a calendar date, only as '1st day of hearing'.
